exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Lateral Surface Area of a Cylinder

question.text: The radius of the base of a cylinder is $3 \: \textrm{ft}$ and its height is $4 \: \textrm{ft}.$ Find the lateral surface area of the cylinder.
question.explanation:
We can calculate the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula

\[ S_L = 2\pi r h, \]

where $r$ is the radius and $h$ is the height of the cylinder.

Substituting $r=3 \,\textrm{ft}$ and $h=4 \,\textrm{ft}$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} S_L &= 2\pi(3) (4) = 24\pi \: \textrm{ft}^2. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Cylinder

question.text: Determine the surface area of the above cylinder.
question.explanation:
We can calculate the surface area of a cylinder using the formula \[ S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh, \]

where $r$ is the radius and $h$ is the height of the cylinder.

Substituting $r=6 \,\textrm{in}$ and $h=14\,\textrm{in}$ into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} S &= 2\pi(6)^2+2\pi(6)(14) \\[3pt] &= 72\pi + 168\pi \\[3pt] &= 240\pi \: \textrm{in}^2. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Dimension of a Cylinder Given Its Surface Area or Lateral Surface Area

question.text: The lateral surface area of a cylinder is $864\pi \: \textrm{cm}^2$ and the ratio of its height to its radius is $3.$ Calculate the radius of the cylinder.
question.explanation:
Let $r$ and $h$ be the radius and height of the cylinder, respectively.

We are given that

\[ \dfrac{h}{r}=3 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad h=3r. \]

We can find the lateral surface area of a cylinder using the formula \[ S_L = 2\pi rh. \]

Substituting the values

\[ S_L=864\pi, \qquad h=3r \]

into the formula for $S_L,$ we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} S_L &= 2\pi r h \\[5pt] 864\pi &= 2\pi r (3r) \\[5pt] 864\pi &= 6\pi r^2 \\[5pt] r^2 &= \dfrac{864\pi}{6\pi} \\[5pt] r^2&= 144 \\[5pt] r&= 12 \: \textrm{cm} \end{align*}

Notice that we disregard the negative solution since length must be positive.

example.title: Finding a Dimension of a Cylinder Given Its Surface Area or Lateral Surface Area

question.text: The surface area of a cylinder is $24\pi \: \textrm{mm}^2$ and the ratio of its radius to its height is $3.$ Calculate the height of the cylinder.
question.explanation:
Let $r$ and $h$ be the radius and height of the cylinder, respectively.

We are given that

\[ \dfrac{r}{h}=3 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad r=3h. \]

We can find the surface area of a cylinder using the formula \[ S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh. \]

Substituting the values

\[ S=24\pi, \qquad r=3h \]

into the formula for $S,$ we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} S &= 2\pi r^2 +2\pi r h \\[5pt] 24\pi &= 2\pi (3h)^2+2\pi (3h) h \\[5pt] 24\pi &= 18 \pi h^2 + 6 \pi h^2 \\[5pt] 24\pi &= 24 \pi h^2 \\[5pt] h^2 &= \dfrac{24\pi}{24\pi} \\[5pt] h^2 &= 1 \\[5pt] h &= 1 \: \textrm{mm} \end{align*}

Notice that we disregard the negative solution since length must be positive.
